# Owen Ford

## Overview

- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v4 c23 P8](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0008), [v4 c23 P9](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0009)</sub>
- **Role:** Writer and author  <sub>[v4 c23 P1](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0001), [v4 c24 P27](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0027), [v4 c25 P0](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

Owen is tall and broad-shouldered, with thick brown hair and a finely-cut nose and chin. He has large, brilliant dark-gray eyes, well-shaped ears, and attractive white teeth when he smiles. Unsmiling, his countenance appears sad and absent, resembling a melancholy hero, but it lights up with mirth, humor, and charm when he smiles.

_Sources: [v4 c23 P8](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0008), [v4 c23 P9](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0009), [v4 c23 P10](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0010)_

## Personality

Owen is a passionate, imaginative, and eloquent creative artist who throws himself heart and soul into his writing. He possesses great humor, charm, and friendly warmth, though he can also experience intense inner agony and deep emotional turmoil. Honesty and moral integrity guide his choices, leading him to accept painful self-sacrifice rather than compromise his principles or betray others. He connects instinctively with empathetic people and easily shares his deepest feelings in times of distress.

_Sources: [v4 c23 P10](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0010), [v4 c25 P9](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0009), [v4 c25 P13](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0013), [v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002), [v4 c26 P5](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0005), [v4 c26 P10](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0010)_

- Imaginative and artistic  <sub>[v4 c25 P11](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0011), [v4 c25 P13](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0013)</sub>

- Novelist and literary writer  <sub>[v4 c25 P0](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0000), [v4 c25 P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006)</sub>

## Goals

- To write a famous novel using Captain Jim's life stories  <sub>[v4 c25 P0](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0000), [v4 c25 P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006)</sub>
- To honor the memory of lost Margaret  <sub>[v4 c25 P2](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0002), [v4 c25 P5](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0005)</sub>

## History

Owen Ford arrives in Four Winds to spend his summer holiday, driven by a desire to visit his mother's childhood home. Upon arriving, he takes up lodging as a summer boarder at Leslie Moore's house. During a visit to Captain Jim's lighthouse, Owen is shown Captain Jim's life-book, which inspires him to collaborate with the old captain and write a major novel based on his life and the story of lost Margaret. He sets up a workshop in a small room at the lighthouse, writing every morning with feverish enthusiasm and spending his afternoons enjoying outings with Anne Blythe, Gilbert, Captain Jim, and Leslie. As the summer progresses, Owen falls deeply in love with Leslie, endowing the female protagonist of his novel with her personality. Near the end of his stay, after finishing his manuscript, he confesses his intense love for Leslie to Anne, expressing heartbreak over Leslie's unhappy marriage while resolving to act honorably and leave in silence. Shortly before his departure, he meets Leslie alone in the garden of the little house, where the two express their mutual love, share a kiss, and crown her hair with a red rose. He later receives Captain Jim's affectionate blessing alongside Leslie, Anne, and Gilbert before leaving Four Winds.

## Background by volume

- His mother was born and raised at Four Winds in the old house built by John Selwyn  <sub>[v4 c23 P11](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0011)</sub>
- He is the grandson of the former schoolmaster of the north shore, who was Captain Jim's dearest friend  <sub>[v4 c25 P7](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0007)</sub>

## Quotes

> You cannot realize how delighted I am to be here, Mrs. Blythe. I have an odd feeling of coming home.  <sub>[v4 c23 P11](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0011)</sub>

> We’ll collaborate. You will give the soul and I the body. Oh, we’ll write a famous book between us, Captain Jim. And we’ll get right to work.  <sub>[v4 c25 P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006)</sub>

> I’m rather glad the doctor is away. I wanted to see you alone, Mrs. Blythe. There is something I must tell somebody, or I think it will drive me mad. I’ve been trying for a week to look it in the face—and I can’t. I know I can trust you—and, besides, you will understand. A woman with eyes like yours always understands. You are one of the folks people instinctively tell things to. Mrs. Blythe, I love Leslie. LOVE her! That seems too weak a word!  <sub>[v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002)</sub>

> These roses are very late—they bloom after all the others have gone—and they hold all the warmth and soul of the summer come to fruition  <sub>[v4 c38 P6](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0006)</sub>

> Love triumphant and perfect. Leslie, you know—you understand. I have loved you from the first. And I KNOW you love me—I don’t need to ask you. But I want to hear you say it—my darling—my darling!  <sub>[v4 c38 P9](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0009)</sub>
